title: Relative projective ideal section sequence from geometric-fibre vanishing
statement:
Let $T$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], $n,d,r\in\mathbf N$, and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X=\mathbf P^n_T$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Put $p:X\to T$, $q=pi$, $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$, $\mathcal O_Z(d)=i^*\mathcal O_X(d)$ and $V_d=\mathcal O_T[x_0,\ldots,x_n]_d$, using the relative twists obtained by gluing the affine-base twists [def-pc-projective-space-twist, def-nagata-relative-projective-space, lem-trf-free-projective-bundle-base-change-space] and ordinary pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Assume $q$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]). For every geometric point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}k\to T$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre], assume that $H^j(Z_{\bar t},\mathcal O_{Z_{\bar t}}(d))=0$ for $j>0$, that $\dim_kH^0(Z_{\bar t},\mathcal O_{Z_{\bar t}}(d))=r$, and that restriction $k[x_0,\ldots,x_n]_d\to H^0(Z_{\bar t},\mathcal O_{Z_{\bar t}}(d))$ is surjective [pqf-def-cohomology]. Then $q$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], $p$ is finitely presented, and $\mathcal I$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent] of finite type (locally generated by finitely many sections). For every $g:T'\to T$, writing $g_X:X'=X\times_TT'\to X$, $i':Z_{T'}\hookrightarrow X'$, and $\mathcal I'=\ker(\mathcal O_{X'}\to i'_*\mathcal O_{Z_{T'}})$, the canonical pullback of the ideal sequence is exact and identifies $g_X^*\mathcal I$ with $\mathcal I'$, compatibly with all twists. The canonical restriction sequence
$$0\longrightarrow K_d=p_*\mathcal I(d)\longrightarrow V_d\longrightarrow E_d=q_*\mathcal O_Z(d)\longrightarrow0$$
is locally split exact, all three terms are finite locally free [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module] (locally finite direct sums of the structure sheaf), and $E_d$ has rank $r$. Under the monomial identification $p_*\mathcal O_X(d)=V_d$, the canonical base-change maps for $K_d$, $p_*\mathcal O_X(d)$ and $E_d$ are isomorphisms for every $g$, and identify the pulled-back sequence with the restriction sequence for $Z_{T'}\subset\mathbf P^n_{T'}$.

source.place: Tags 0B9S (lemma-open-where-cohomology-in-degree-i-rank-r-geometric), 0B91 (lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general), 01XT (lemma-cohomology-projective-space-over-ring); flat-closed-family ideal base change and split-kernel argument from the returned proof, steps 1, 4--6

proof.text: Use the coordinate-preserving comparison between base-change projective space and relative projective space. Over each affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$, its standard opens have rings $A[x_j/x_i:j\ne i]$, polynomial algebras with $n$ generators and no relations. They exhibit $p$ as locally of finite presentation. The projective-space properness lemma makes $p$ proper, hence quasi-compact and separated. Its diagonal is a closed immersion, hence affine and quasi-compact by affine permanence; thus $p$ is quasi-separated and finitely presented. Apply the flat-projective-twist lemma to $i$ and $q$: $q$ is proper and $F=\mathcal O_Z(d)$ is an invertible, finitely presented module flat over $T$. The same lemma identifies every pullback of $F$ with the twist on the corresponding closed family.

source.place: Tags 01NE (lemma-projective-space), 01NH (lemma-projective-space-separated); morphisms.tex Tag 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper); standard charts and polynomial presentations

proof.text: Apply the flat-closed-family ideal lemma, now that both $p$ and $q$ are finitely presented and $q$ is flat. It gives quasi-coherence and finite type of $\mathcal I$ and, for every $g$, the exact pulled-back ideal sequence and its canonical kernel identification. Tensoring with $\mathcal O_X(d)$ preserves this sequence: on an open where the twist has a rank-one basis, tensoring is the identity on the underlying sequence. On such an open the quotient is $i_*\mathcal O_Z(d)$, since the same basis restricts to $Z$; these identifications agree on overlaps, where both bases are multiplied by the same transition unit. On $X'$ the same holds: over affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq T'$ mapping into $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$, the coordinate-preserving comparison identifies the standard charts compatibly with the coefficient map $A\to B$, so $g_X^*$ carries each basis $e_i^{(d)}$ and transition rule $e_i^{(d)}=(x_i/x_j)^de_j^{(d)}$ to those of $\mathcal O_{X'}(d)$; hence $g_X^*\mathcal O_X(d)\cong\mathcal O_{X'}(d)$, and with the twist-pullback identification of step 1 on $Z$, tensoring the pulled-back ideal sequence gives $g_X^*(\mathcal I(d))\cong\mathcal I'(d)$ and quotient $i'_*\mathcal O_{Z_{T'}}(d)$. This proves the asserted ideal comparison compatibly with twists. For each open $W\subseteq T$, sections over $p^{-1}W$ preserve kernels, so the twisted ideal sequence identifies $p_*\mathcal I(d)$ with the kernel of $p_*\mathcal O_X(d)\to q_*F$.

source.place: Tags 02FV (lemma-finite-presentation-permanence), 01TV (lemma-closed-immersion-finite-presentation); algebra.tex Tag 00HL (lemma-flat-tor-zero); tensoring in a rank-one trivialization

proof.text: Apply the open-locus theorem to $(q,F)$ with $(i,r)=(0,r)$, obtaining an open $U\subseteq T$. For each geometric $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}k\to T$, the derived cohomology model identifies the nonnegative cohomology of $Rq_{\bar t,*}F_{\bar t}$ with the assumed fibre cohomology, and gives zero in negative degrees. These sheaves on the one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ are zero away from degree zero and degree zero is $k^r$. The single-cohomology derived-category lemma therefore makes this object a rank-$r$ free module in degree zero. The defining equivalence of the open-locus theorem implies that every $\bar t$ factors through $U$. Each point of $T$ admits an algebraically closed residue extension, so $|U|=|T|$ and the open subscheme $U$ is $T$. Applying the equivalence to $\mathrm{id}_T$ and taking degree-zero cohomology gives $Rq_*F\cong E_d[0]$, where $E_d=q_*F$ is finite locally free of rank $r$.

source.place: Tag 0B9S (lemma-open-where-cohomology-in-degree-i-rank-r-geometric), using the geometric-point test and the degree-zero case

proof.text: The canonical derived module base-change isomorphism for $(q,F)$ is supplied by the proper-flat perfect-direct-image theorem. Since step 3 identifies $Rq_*F$ with $E_d[0]$, locally a finite free module in degree zero, the flat-complex pullback theorem computes $Lg^*Rq_*F$ as $(g^*E_d)[0]$. Taking $H^0$ gives an isomorphism $g^*E_d\to q'_*F'$ for every $g$. This is the canonical ordinary section base-change map: in the definition of the derived module comparison, the unit is the ordinary tensor-pullback unit and the derived-to-ordinary comparison is its transpose. On degree-zero sections that unit sends $s$ to $1\otimes s$; after scalar multiplication the map sends $b\otimes s$ to $b\,g_Z^*s$. Thus the isomorphism is the restriction/pullback comparison in the statement, rather than an unspecified isomorphism of modules.

source.place: Tag 0B91 (lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general), part (2); canonical comparison as in Tag 0A1H (lemma-base-change-tensor-perfect)

proof.text: On every affine base open $\operatorname{Spec}A$, the projective-twist cohomology formula identifies $\Gamma(\mathbf P^n_A,\mathcal O(d))$ with the degree-$d$ polynomials. The identification sends the monomial $x^e$ to the section represented by $x^e/x_i^d$ in the standard rank-one basis on $D_+(x_i)$. Hence restriction in $A$ and any coefficient map $A\to B$ preserve this identification: both send each coefficient $a_e$ to its image and fix the monomials. They glue to the monomial identification $p_*\mathcal O_X(d)=V_d$, and the canonical base-change map is the isomorphism $B\otimes_A A[x_0,\ldots,x_n]_d\to B[x_0,\ldots,x_n]_d$. In particular $V_d$ is free of finite rank $N=\binom{n+d}{n}$. For $n=0$, use the formula's separate rank-one case: $a x_0^d$ corresponds to $a$ on $\operatorname{Spec}A$, so the same assertion holds.

source.place: Tag 01XT (lemma-cohomology-projective-space-over-ring), degree zero for d nonnegative; standard monomial representatives

proof.text: Let $\alpha:V_d\to E_d$ be restriction. Its geometric fibre is the map in the hypothesis: steps 4 and 5 compute the two base-change maps by pulling back sections, and restriction to $Z$ commutes with that pullback. Fix $t\in T$ and trivialize $E_d$ and $V_d$ near $t$. If $r>0$, geometric surjectivity says that the $r\times N$ matrix of $\alpha$ has an $r\times r$ minor with nonzero determinant in the algebraically closed field at $t$. Its determinant is therefore nonzero already in $\kappa(t)$; shrink to the open where that determinant is invertible. After permuting columns and multiplying on the left by the inverse minor, the matrix is $[I_r\ C]$. It has section $y\mapsto(y,0)$ and kernel freely parametrized by $z\mapsto(-Cz,z)$. If $r=0$ the target is zero and the assertion is immediate. Thus $\alpha$ is surjective and its kernel is finite locally free, locally of rank $N-r$. Step 2 identifies that kernel with $K_d$, proving the locally split exact restriction sequence. (If $T$ is nonempty the minor argument also forces $r\leq N$.)

source.place: Tag 01C6 (definition-locally-free); explicit invertible-minor calculation, no reducedness or Noetherian hypothesis

proof.text: Fix any $g:T'\to T$. On inverse images of the splitting opens of step 6, ordinary pullback preserves the displayed split sequence, because it sends the two inclusion/projection identities to the same identities. The canonical maps from its three terms to the sequence of the base-changed family form a commuting diagram: a local pure tensor $b\otimes s$ maps to $b$ times the pulled-back section, and restriction to $Z_{T'}$ commutes with this formula. Step 2 identifies the pulled-back twisted ideal with the actual ideal twist on $X'$. Sections preserve its kernel, so the bottom kernel is $p'_*\mathcal I'(d)$. The middle and right vertical maps are the canonical isomorphisms from steps 5 and 4. They identify their kernels, hence the left vertical map $g^*K_d\to p'_*\mathcal I'(d)$ is an isomorphism too. This proves all three canonical section base-change assertions and identifies the whole pulled-back sequence with the restriction sequence on $T'$.
